title: Using the map instead of your memory
target: How to use the R.E.P.O. map so the crew stops relying on memory, using the markers and the reveal behaviour the game already provides.
version: R.E.P.O. v0.4.0, as installed for this build (see the sources page for the exact version string)
prerequisites: The map open to at least one member of the crew
A crew that says what it finds rather than keeping it quiet

steps.do: Open the map early rather than at the moment you are lost.
steps.because: the map fills in over time with its own spacing and waits (MapBacktrack)

steps.do: Call a valuable out as soon as it shows, instead of carrying it in silence.
steps.because: valuables get a map marker with a small and a large version (MapValuable)

steps.do: Use the map to keep track of the crew as well as the loot.
steps.because: the player has a marker of its own on the map (DirtFinderMapPlayer)

steps.do: Watch the map for monsters instead of only listening for them.
steps.because: monsters have their own marker on the map (DirtFinderMapEnemy)

steps.do: Do not read a dark patch as an empty room.
steps.because: the map starts dark and fills in behind you (DirtFinderMapScanlines)

commonMistakes: Relying on memory for a layout you have only walked through once.
Assuming a dark part of the map contains nothing.
Carrying a valuable in without telling anyone it exists.
sources: This installation of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
